UnitStatement: The amendment purpose is to extend Chirality App so it can safely orchestrate deterministic domain engines without becoming those engines.
The amendment adds a Domain Engine Integration capability to Chirality App.
Chirality remains a local-first desktop harness for governed agents, deliverables, filesystem-native project state, lifecycle records, dependency registers, deterministic tools, and human review.
Chirality does not become a domain-specific engineering application, solver, CAD tool, stress-analysis engine, or professional prover.
The reusable integration pattern separates Chirality App, Domain Engine, and Human Operator roles.
A Domain Engine is deterministic specialist software that owns its domain model and computation.
For OpenPipeStress, Chirality orchestrates, documents, summarizes, reconciles, and governs.
OpenPipeStress owns the piping model, GUI, solver, model states, analysis runs, comparisons, and handoff packages.
An external professional stress tool validates OpenPipeStress work for reliance.
The responsible engineer accepts OpenPipeStress work.
OpenPipeStress is the first concrete domain-engine integration while Chirality preserves generality for future domain tools.
Chirality App PRD defines a local desktop harness for governed AI agents operating against a selected filesystem working root.
Chirality stores project truth in git-tracked files and retains human authority at gates.
OpenPipeStress v0.2 defines an analysis-grade piping design engine with an analytical stress-analysis core and schema-backed physical model.
OpenPipeStress v0.2 includes model states, analysis runs, comparison records, and handoff packages.
The agreed Chirality and OpenPipeStress integration model is federated rather than monolithic.
Chirality does not embed or replace OpenPipeStress.
OpenPipeStress does not become a general-purpose agent operating system.
Agents do not directly mutate canonical engineering model states.
Integration occurs through deterministic tools, manifests, operation proposals, summaries, reports, and human-gated workflows.
Chirality should add support for Domain Engine Profiles and Domain Tool Adapters.
A Domain Engine Profile identifies what domain engine is present.
A Domain Engine Profile identifies authoritative domain artifacts and generated summaries or manifests.
A Domain Engine Profile identifies paths protected from direct agent writes and paths agents may write to.
A Domain Engine Profile identifies available deterministic tools, safe tool outputs, and required human gates.
A Domain Tool Adapter exposes deterministic commands from a domain engine to Chirality.
A Domain Tool Adapter may validate models, summarize model state, run analysis, compare states, produce report fragments, or generate handoff manifests.
A Domain Tool Adapter must not allow agents to bypass domain-engine validation or human authority.
A domain engine is specialist software that owns domain-specific models, calculations, validation, and graphical or technical workflows.
OpenPipeStress is an example domain engine for piping design and stress-analysis model authoring.
A Domain Engine Profile describes how Chirality may discover, read, invoke, summarize, and govern a domain engine inside a working root.
A Domain Tool Adapter is a deterministic command-line or API surface provided by the domain engine and callable by Chirality.
An Authoritative Domain Artifact represents domain truth owned by the domain engine.
Agents must not directly edit Authoritative Domain Artifacts unless the domain profile explicitly permits a narrow safe action.
OpenPipeStress authoritative artifacts include project.ops.yaml, states, runs, comparisons, handoff, canonical model files, and analysis result files.
A Chirality-Readable Artifact is a summary, manifest, report fragment, warning list, assumption register, delta table, or checklist that agents may read, summarize, reconcile, or cite.
An Agent-Writable Artifact is a file that agents may create or modify under explicit write scope.
Agent-writable artifact examples include operation proposals, review notes, TBD registers, draft report sections, handoff checklists, dependency registers, and reconciliation notes.
A Protected Write Path is a path that agents may not directly modify.
Changes to protected domain artifacts must occur only through the domain engine, a deterministic adapter command, or an explicitly human-approved operation.
An Operation Proposal is a structured proposed domain-model change.
An Operation Proposal is not accepted model truth and remains a draft artifact for human review and domain-engine validation.
Chirality should support local deterministic domain-engine integrations through file-based profiles, tool adapters, manifests, protected write paths, and human-gated operation proposals.
Chirality should preserve its role as a governed agent harness rather than a domain computation engine.
The Domain Engine Integration goal extends Chirality current deterministic tool registry and filesystem-native project truth model.
Chirality must not become a domain-specific engineering solver, CAD system, piping stress analysis program, or professional validation or prover tool.
Chirality must not directly edit canonical domain-engine model states unless a safe deterministic operation is exposed and the required human gate is satisfied.
Chirality must not treat agent-generated domain advice as accepted engineering work.
Chirality must not declare domain-specific professional acceptance, code compliance, certification, sealing, or approval.
Chirality must not parse or normalize proprietary third-party engineering software outputs unless a specific adapter is scoped, implemented, and validated.
Chirality must not store authoritative domain truth in hidden chat state, transient session memory, vendor systems, or untracked UI state.
Chirality must not bypass the domain engine schema validation, solver validation, or professional-boundary notices.
When a domain engine is integrated, the domain engine remains the owner of its canonical model and calculation records.
Chirality may orchestrate, summarize, and govern work around an integrated domain engine.
Agents may draft operation proposals, review notes, and summaries.
Domain-engine tools validate and compute.
Humans accept or reject changes and decide what can be relied upon.
Agents must not improvise domain results.
Agents must rely on deterministic tool outputs, manifests, logs, reports, and explicitly cited project files.
Canonical domain model files, model states, analysis runs, result files, comparison records, and handoff packages are protected unless the domain profile permits a specific deterministic write path.
Every domain-engine integration should generate bounded human-readable and machine-readable artifacts.
Chirality should reason about domain work without needing to own domain internals.
Domain Engine Profile registry is in scope for Chirality when the amendment is adopted.
Domain Tool Adapter discovery is in scope for Chirality when the amendment is adopted.
Domain artifact scanning inside the working root is in scope for Chirality when the amendment is adopted.
Profile-defined protected write paths are in scope for Chirality when the amendment is adopted.
Profile-defined agent-writable paths are in scope for Chirality when the amendment is adopted.
Deterministic invocation of approved domain tools is in scope for Chirality when the amendment is adopted.
Domain tool result capture as bounded summaries, manifests, CSVs, Markdown files, and JSON or YAML records is in scope.
Agent creation of operation proposals and review notes is in scope for Chirality when the amendment is adopted.
Human-gated application of domain operations is in scope for Chirality when the amendment is adopted.
Domain-specific professional-boundary notices are in scope for Chirality when the amendment is adopted.
Domain-specific IP/data-boundary review checklists are in scope where applicable.
Embedding the OpenPipeStress 3D GUI inside Chirality remains out of scope unless separately amended.
Implementing the OpenPipeStress solver inside Chirality remains out of scope unless separately amended.
Directly editing OpenPipeStress canonical model-state files from agents remains out of scope unless separately amended.
Parsing CAESAR II, AutoPIPE, or other commercial stress-analysis result files remains out of scope unless separately amended.
Declaring external prover validation complete remains out of scope unless separately amended.
Issuing professional approval, code compliance, or ready-for-construction status remains out of scope unless separately amended.
Network-based vendor integrations outside Chirality approved network policy remain out of scope unless separately amended.
Cloud storage of domain model truth remains out of scope unless separately amended.
Chirality shall support a Domain Engine Profile schema declaring engine metadata, root paths, artifacts, write boundaries, deterministic tools, and required human gates.
Chirality shall validate domain profiles before use, failing invalid profiles with typed errors and not silently downgrading protected paths.
Chirality shall distinguish authoritative domain artifacts from Chirality-readable artifacts in UI and agent context.
Chirality shall enforce protected domain write paths at tool-invocation and agent-write boundaries where implemented.
Chirality shall allow agents to write only profile-permitted proposal and review paths.
Domain tool calls shall be deterministic and bounded, with structured, size-limited, logged output.
Domain tool calls shall not rely on hidden app state for authoritative project truth.
Domain tool results shall be captured as project files when they affect project reasoning.
Chirality shall expose domain artifacts in working-root scans.
Chirality shall expose approved domain tools through a deterministic tool registry or equivalent domain-tool registry.
Agents shall invoke only declared domain tools with declared input and output contracts.
Chirality shall support operation proposal files.
Chirality shall support human approval metadata for domain operation application where tool-supported.
Applied operations can bind approval reference, user identity where available, timestamp, source proposal, and resulting domain artifact hash.
Chirality shall support domain professional-boundary notices.
Chirality shall support domain IP/data-boundary checks where a profile defines them.
Chirality shall support domain profile UI panels for profile status, protected paths, available tools, latest summaries, warnings, and proposals.
Chirality shall support launch or deep-link actions into domain applications where supported.
Chirality shall support future external result states as domain-readable artifacts.
External results can be represented as structured artifacts and compared by the domain engine without Chirality declaring professional validation.
The proposed GET /api/domain/profiles/list endpoint lists domain profiles available in the working root and bundled instruction root.
The proposed POST /api/domain/profile/validate endpoint validates a domain engine profile.
The proposed GET /api/domain/artifacts/scan endpoint scans the selected working root for domain-engine artifacts declared by active profiles.
The proposed POST /api/domain/tool/invoke endpoint invokes a declared deterministic domain tool with validated arguments.
The proposed GET /api/domain/proposals/list endpoint lists operation proposals for a selected domain engine.
The proposed POST /api/domain/proposal/validate endpoint validates an operation proposal against profile schema and domain-engine validation where available.
Any endpoint that writes or mutates authoritative domain artifacts must be separately reviewed and must respect human-gate requirements.
A minimal Domain Engine Profile should include schema_version, id, name, engine_type, and profile_version fields.
The example profile uses domain_root_patterns to identify OpenPipeStress directories in a working root.
The example profile treats OpenPipeStress project.ops.yaml, states, runs, comparisons, and handoff paths as authoritative artifacts.
The example profile treats model manifests, run and comparison summaries, delta tables, handoff manifests, export warnings, and TBD registers as Chirality-readable artifacts.
The example profile protects OpenPipeStress project.ops.yaml, states, runs, comparisons, and handoff paths from direct writes.
The example profile allows agents to write OpenPipeStress proposals, Review_Notes.md, TBD_Register.md, and Draft_Report_Sections.
The example profile declares deterministic tools by id and mode.
The example profile marks ops.validate_model, ops.summarize_model, ops.list_states, and ops.list_runs as read-only tools.
The example profile marks ops.run_analysis, ops.compare_states, ops.compare_runs, and ops.generate_handoff as domain-controlled write tools.
The example profile requires human confirmation for ops.run_analysis.
The example profile requires human confirmation for ops.generate_handoff.
The example profile marks ops.generate_report_fragment as read_only_or_summary_write.
The example profile marks ops.check_boundary_language and ops.check_private_data_boundary as read-only tools.
A domain profile can define professional-boundary claims that agents must not make.

The example professional boundary prohibits claims of code compliance for reliance, professional approval, certification, sealing, ready-for-construction status, or external prover validation without external human record.

OpenPipeStress should provide model summarization.
OpenPipeStress should provide state and run enumeration.
OpenPipeStress should provide internal analysis runs.
OpenPipeStress should provide deterministic comparisons.
OpenPipeStress should provide operation proposals.
OpenPipeStress should provide handoff package generation.
OpenPipeStress should provide report fragments.
OpenPipeStress should provide IP/data-boundary checks.
OpenPipeStress should provide professional-boundary language checks.

Chirality may read model manifests, state summaries, analysis-run summaries, warning lists, assumption registers, comparison summaries, delta tables, handoff manifests, draft report fragments, operation proposals, review notes, and TBD registers.

Chirality agents must not directly write canonical OpenPipeStress project files, accepted model states, analysis run records, comparison records, handoff internals, solver outputs, or professional acceptance records.

Chirality agents may write operation proposals, review notes, TBD registers, scope notes, handoff checklists, draft report sections, dependency register entries, change records, and reconciliation notes when inside declared agent-writable paths.
The suggested OpenPipeStress project root layout includes INIT.md, a piping design package, sources, reconciliation, change, and archive areas.
The suggested piping design package includes deliverables for design basis, OpenPipeStress model, internal stress analysis, state comparison, and external prover handoff.
The suggested OpenPipeStress model deliverable contains model manifest files, warnings, assumptions, and OpenPipeStress project folders.
The suggested internal stress analysis deliverable contains run summaries and solver diagnostics.
The suggested state comparison deliverable contains comparison summary, delta table, and review notes.
The suggested external prover handoff deliverable contains a handoff manifest, export warnings, and external review TBDs.
Agents operating under a domain profile must not fabricate domain results.
Agents operating under a domain profile must not directly mutate protected domain artifacts.
Agents operating under a domain profile must not invent missing engineering data.
Agents operating under a domain profile must treat unknowns as TBD.
Agents operating under a domain profile must use deterministic tool outputs as evidence.
Agents operating under a domain profile must cite model state IDs, run IDs, comparison IDs, manifest hashes, and file paths where available.
Agents operating under a domain profile must write proposals, not accepted changes.
Agents operating under a domain profile must preserve professional-boundary language.
Agents operating under a domain profile must preserve IP/data-boundary language.
Agents must request or record human review when a proposed action would affect relied-upon project state.

The Domain Engine Integration feature should be tested for write-scope enforcement and proposal file creation.
The Domain Engine Integration feature should be tested for rejection of direct writes to protected domain artifacts.
The Domain Engine Integration feature should be tested for handling a missing domain engine executable.
The Domain Engine Integration feature should be tested for handling an invalid domain model.
The Domain Engine Integration feature should be tested for handling large domain outputs.

The Domain Engine Integration feature should be tested for professional-boundary language checks.
The Domain Engine Integration feature should be tested for deterministic output on repeated tool calls.
The risk that agents directly modify engineering model truth is mitigated by protected write paths, deterministic tools, operation proposals, and human gates.
The risk that Chirality is mistaken for a domain solver is mitigated by product language that Chirality orchestrates and governs while the domain engine computes.
The risk that agent summaries misrepresent technical results is mitigated by deterministic tool outputs, bounded summaries, and citations to manifests, runs, and comparisons.
The risk that domain tools expose private data to chat unnecessarily is mitigated by redaction, summary controls, and private-data boundary checks.
The risk that operation proposals are mistaken for accepted model changes is mitigated by clear labels and human-approved application by the domain engine.
The risk that professional status labels imply approval is mitigated by prohibiting automatic code-compliant, certified, approved, and ready-for-construction labels.
The risk that the domain profile overfits to OpenPipeStress is mitigated by defining a generic Domain Engine Profile with OpenPipeStress as the first example.
The risk that integration expands current release scope too much is mitigated by treating it as amendment or future scope unless explicitly added to a release decomposition.
The Domain Engine Integration amendment should be implemented in stages.
Stage A deliverables include the amendment, DOMAIN_ENGINE_PROFILE_SPEC.md, an OpenPipeStress example profile, path and write-boundary policy, and operation proposal schema.
Stage B deliverables include profile validation, artifact scanning, manifest ingestion, read-only tool invocation, and agent access to generated summaries.
Stage C deliverables include approved tool invocation registry, deterministic result capture, analysis-run and comparison generation through the adapter, and domain-controlled tool outputs.
Stage D deliverables include proposal authoring, proposal validation, diff preview, human approval metadata, and optional apply operation through the domain engine.
Stage E deliverables include a profile status panel, launch actions, proposal browser, and domain artifact summary dashboard.

The PRD product summary should state that Chirality governs agent work, deliverables, manifests, review notes, and human gates while the domain engine owns domain-specific model truth and computation.
The PRD in-scope text should add Domain Engine Profile support for local deterministic specialist tools.
The PRD in-scope text should include profile validation, protected write paths, agent-writable proposal paths, domain tool invocation, and generated manifests or summaries.
The PRD out-of-scope text should state that Chirality does not become the domain engine.
The PRD out-of-scope text should state that Chirality does not directly solve, certify, approve, or professionally validate domain-specific engineering work.
The PRD out-of-scope text should state that Chirality does not allow agents to directly modify protected domain model artifacts.

The amendment is adopted when the Chirality PRD includes domain-engine integration as an explicit future or active scope item.
The amendment is adopted when a Domain Engine Profile schema exists.
The amendment is adopted when OpenPipeStress has a draft profile using the Domain Engine Profile schema.
The amendment is adopted when protected write paths and agent-writable paths are clearly defined.
The amendment is adopted when the PRD states that Chirality does not become the domain solver or professional prover.
The amendment is adopted when the PRD states that domain operations require deterministic tools and human gates.
The amendment is adopted when future implementation work can be decomposed into profile validation, artifact scanning, tool invocation, and proposal workflows.
Chirality is the governed professional-work harness, domain engines are deterministic specialist tools, agents create proposals and organize evidence, and humans decide what can be relied upon.
